records.note: No prison-housing placement data for trans prisoners in New Brunswick was found. The mandated single enwiki full-text search returned no New Brunswick-specific prison content; the top relevant hit, Wikipedia's 'Transgender rights in Canada' (fetched, HTTP 200, cached research/fetched/fa4b580edec2aa33.txt), covers New Brunswick only for legal gender-marker change (2017 amendment adding gender identity/expression to human-rights law; Service New Brunswick change-of-sex certificates) and contains nothing on custody placement - no birth-sex-vs-identity housing rule, no trans special unit, no solitary/segregation practice for trans prisoners in provincial jails, and no documented case or ruling. No New Brunswick-specific known-good source (PRI/HRW/ILGA/news) could be verified within the fetch budget; no usable finding.

No prison-housing placement data for trans prisoners in Mexico City (Distrito Federal) was found. The mandated single enwiki full-text search returned no trans-placement content; the top hit, Wikipedia's 'LGBTQ people in prison' (fetched, HTTP 200, cached research/fetched/58ce7836f80217d1.txt), covers Mexico only for same-sex conjugal visits in Mexico City prisons (allowed from July 2007 after a push by the CDHDF, per Mexico City's 2003 anti-discrimination law) - no housing-placement rule (birth-sex vs identity), no trans special unit, and no solitary/segregation practice for trans prisoners is described. A second known-good attempt (Penal Reform International prison-conditions page) contained no transgender content, and no Mexico City-specific source (PRI/HRW/ILGA/news, incl. the documented placements and court transfers of trans women in CDMX prisons) could be verified within the fetch budget; no usable finding.
